edition.authority: Council of Vienne under Clement V
edition.notes: A catalog-level identification of the conventional received Latin text of the errors and censure. Denzinger prints the listed propositions as condemned errors, not as teaching; consumers must not quote a listed proposition as a doctrinal statement. No exact artifact of a printed Denzinger edition is retained or hashed. The 1312 conciliar act is public domain; particular printed editions of Denzinger retain their own editorial rights.
edition.publication: Latin text of the constitution as printed in Denzinger's Enchiridion symbolorum, nn. 891-899 (older numbering 471-478), the eight listed errors with the concluding censure
edition.title: Ad nostrum qui — Latin text as received in Denzinger's Enchiridion symbolorum

alternate_titles: On the errors of the Beghards and Beguines
work.author: Council of Vienne under Clement V
work.description: The constitution of the Council of Vienne, session III (6 May 1312), listing and condemning eight errors of the Beghards and Beguines on the state of perfection, including the proposition that every intellectual nature is naturally blessed in itself and that the soul does not need the light of glory elevating it to see God and enjoy him blessedly.
work.title: Ad nostrum qui
